policies.rationale: Restates the raw intent as the root declarative policy: the robot must bring the stovetop surface to a clean state.
Before cleaning can begin the robot must assess the current state of the stovetop to determine what contaminants, obstacles, or hazards are present.

constraints.resource: stovetop surface geometry and thermal map

policies.rationale: Scanning the surface with vision and thermal sensors captures the spatial layout of debris zones and identifies hot burner areas before any physical contact.
Each detected region must be classified by type (grease, food residue, liquid spill, loose debris, hot zone) so that the correct cleaning method can be selected.
Detecting whether any burner is active or above safe-contact temperature is a prerequisite safety check that gates all subsequent physical actions.
A plan must be decided that orders the cleaning sub-tasks (hazard mitigation, loose debris removal, wet wiping, drying) into a safe and complete sequence before execution begins.
Continuous monitoring of temperature, force, and surface state throughout execution is required to detect unsafe conditions and verify progress toward a clean stovetop.
Based on detected burner temperatures the plan must decide whether to proceed immediately, wait for cooling, or flag the burner as a no-contact zone before any wiping begins.

constraints.resource: robot arm motion toward burner zone
constraints.spatial: hot burner zone (surface temperature above safe threshold)

policies.rationale: Fires when a burner surface temperature exceeds the safe-contact threshold; halting arm motion prevents burns to the robot end-effector and avoids spreading heated contaminants.

constraints.resource: burner zone region in task map

policies.rationale: Fires when a burner is confirmed above safe temperature; flagging the zone in the task map ensures the planner routes all wiping paths around it until it cools.

constraints.spatial: stovetop surface zones (loose-debris, grease, liquid, safe-to-contact)

policies.rationale: Classified regions must be sequenced into ordered sub-tasks so that loose debris is removed before wet wiping, preventing smearing, and grease zones receive appropriate treatment.
Loose debris must be swept or brushed off before any wet cloth contacts the surface to prevent particles from being ground into the surface or smeared into grease.

constraints.resource: robot arm with dry brush or scraper end-effector
constraints.spatial: edge of loose-debris zone on stovetop

policies.rationale: The arm must be positioned at the far edge of the debris zone so that the sweeping stroke moves debris toward the stovetop edge and into a collection area.

constraints.spatial: loose-debris zone toward stovetop collection edge

policies.rationale: Fires after arm is positioned; executes a controlled lateral sweep stroke to consolidate and move loose debris off the active cooking surface.

constraints.spatial: stovetop collection edge or adjacent counter

policies.rationale: Fires after sweeping; collects consolidated debris into a receptacle so it does not fall back onto the stovetop or onto the floor.

constraints.spatial: grease and residue zones on stovetop

policies.rationale: Grease and baked-on residue require a wet cleaning agent and dwell time before wiping, which must be planned as a distinct sub-task sequence separate from loose debris removal.

constraints.resource: cleaning agent (food-safe degreaser or diluted dish soap)

policies.rationale: A food-safe cleaning agent appropriate for grease must be selected from storage before application to ensure surface safety and cleaning efficacy.

constraints.spatial: grease and residue zones on stovetop

policies.rationale: Fires after agent selection; applies a controlled amount of cleaning agent to the grease zones to begin chemical breakdown of the residue before mechanical wiping.

constraints.resource: applied cleaning agent on grease zones
constraints.spatial: grease and residue zones on stovetop

policies.rationale: Fires after agent application; pausing for a dwell period allows the cleaning agent to chemically loosen grease before mechanical wiping, reducing required scrub force.

constraints.spatial: grease and residue zones on stovetop

policies.rationale: Fires after dwell; applies controlled circular or linear scrubbing motion with a damp cloth or sponge end-effector to mechanically lift loosened grease from the surface.
Liquid spills require blotting before wiping to prevent spreading, and must be planned as a distinct sub-task to avoid enlarging the contaminated area.
Fires when a liquid spill zone is reached; blotting absorbs bulk liquid before wiping to prevent spreading the spill across clean areas of the stovetop.
Fires after blotting; wipes the residual moisture and dissolved contaminants from the zone using a clean damp cloth in inward strokes to avoid re-contaminating adjacent areas.

constraints.resource: entire stovetop surface after zone cleaning

policies.rationale: After all zone-specific cleaning sub-tasks are complete, a final full-surface wipe and dry pass must be planned to achieve a uniformly clean and streak-free result.
Fires after all zone sub-tasks complete; executes a systematic overlapping wipe pattern across the full safe surface to remove any remaining residue and cleaning agent.
Fires after the final wipe; drying the surface with a clean dry cloth removes residual moisture to prevent water spots and leave the stovetop in a clean, dry state.
After execution the surface must be evaluated against a cleanliness criterion to confirm the intent has been satisfied or to identify zones requiring a repeat cleaning pass.
The post-cleaning surface scan is compared against the cleanliness threshold to produce a pass or fail verdict for each surface zone.
For any zone that fails the cleanliness comparison, the planner must decide whether to trigger a repeat cleaning pass or escalate to the human operator.

constraints.resource: cleaning action sequence for failed zone

policies.rationale: Fires when a zone fails the cleanliness check and a retry is within the allowed attempt count; re-executes the appropriate cleaning sub-task for that zone.

constraints.resource: human operator alert with zone failure details

policies.rationale: Fires when retry attempts are exhausted or the zone cannot be cleaned safely by the robot; notifying the human operator ensures the task is completed without leaving the stovetop in a degraded state.

constraints.spatial: robot end-effector contact point on stovetop

policies.rationale: Force feedback must be compared against safe contact-force limits throughout execution to detect unexpected resistance that could indicate a fragile surface feature or an obstacle.

constraints.spatial: contact point where force limit is exceeded

policies.rationale: Fires when measured contact force exceeds the safe threshold; retracting the arm immediately prevents damage to the stovetop surface or the robot end-effector.

constraints.resource: obstacle or fragile-feature region in task map
constraints.spatial: contact point where force limit was exceeded

policies.rationale: Fires after arm retraction; flags the location in the task map so the planner reroutes subsequent wipe strokes around the anomalous region.
